item.title: Critical Ruby Heap Overflow Exploit (ruby2shell) Disclosed in String Case Conversion
item.description:
Critical Ruby Heap Overflow Exploit (ruby2shell) Disclosed in String Case Conversion

🔍 Overview

On November 19, 2026, the Ruby programming language team disclosed ruby2shell (CVE-2026-132825), a critical heap buffer overflow vulnerability in how Ruby handles string case conversion. The flaw allows remote code execution in certain scenarios, particularly when processing strings in legacy single-byte encodings like ISO-8859-1 and Windows-1252.

🧩 How it works

The vulnerability arises due to how Ruby processes strings containing special characters, such as the German sharp s (ß). In single-byte encodings, the uppercase form of this character is represented as two bytes (‘SS’ in ASCII), but Ruby’s case conversion logic incorrectly assumes the output will match the input length. When converting case for strings with 21 or more sharp s characters, Ruby writes two bytes but checks for only one, causing a buffer overflow.

In UTF-8, this issue does not occur because the encoding handles multi-byte characters differently, but legacy systems still rely on single-byte encodings.

⚙️ Key details

  • Severity: Critical (Ruby rates it as such).
  • Affected versions: Ruby 3.3.x up to 3.3.13, 3.4.x up to 3.4.12, and 4.0.x up to 4.0.9.
  • Fixed versions: Ruby 3.3.14, 3.4.13, and 4.0.10 (also patching six additional memory safety flaws, some of which can lead to code execution).
  • Exploit paths: Affected by default in Ruby on Rails and classic-style Sinatra applications via HTML forms (GET/POST requests). Other frameworks (Rack, non-classic Sinatra) are not exposed by default.
  • Self-hosted products: Bundled Ruby versions in GitLab, GitHub Enterprise Server, Mastodon, OpenProject, Discourse, and Chatwoot shipped vulnerable versions in their latest releases at disclosure.
  • Cloudflare WAF: Blocks ruby2shell and a related integer overflow (GHSA-87fm-7w84-j2px) in both Free and Managed Rulesets, with Block as default action. This is a compensating control, not a replacement for patching.

🚀 Availability

  • Veria Labs reported affected default configurations in Ruby on Rails and classic Sinatra before authentication.
  • Cloudflare WAF updates added rules to block both ruby2shell and GHSA-87fm-7w84-j2px.
  • Cloudflare patched its own Ruby-based systems and found no signs of compromise.
  • Scanning for exploits is expected to begin shortly after disclosure.

💡 Why it matters

  • Exploitation risk: The vulnerability can lead to remote code execution, posing a severe threat to systems relying on vulnerable Ruby versions.
  • Patch delays: Upgrading bundled Ruby in self-hosted products or container images can be time-consuming, leaving systems exposed.
  • Legacy encodings: The issue highlights risks in supporting outdated single-byte encodings alongside UTF-8.
  • WAF limitations: While Cloudflare’s WAF reduces exposure, exploits may still bypass it through unmonitored paths.

⚠️ Recommendations

  • Immediate action: Upgrade Ruby to the patched versions (3.3.14, 3.4.13, or 4.0.10) or apply backported fixes in distribution packages.
  • Monitor for scans: Expect increased scanning activity post-disclosure.
  • Verify package versions: Check full package versions against distribution advisories to confirm fixes.
  • Cloudflare WAF: Use as a temporary mitigant while patching, but do not rely solely on it.

📊 Additional vulnerabilities fixed in the same releases:

Vulnerability ID Description Engine Affected
GHSA-87fm-7w84-j2px Integer overflow in string case conversion String case conversion
(Five others) Memory safety flaws in Ruby’s regex engine Regular expressions

#security #ruby #heap-overflow #remote-code-execution #vulnerability-patch

Source: How Cloudflare WAF protects against ruby2shell (CVE-2026-132825)

item.title: Critical PHP and Drupal Security Updates Released
item.description:
Critical PHP and Drupal Security Updates Released

On November 19, security updates were released for 18 vulnerabilities in the PHP development ecosystem, alongside the patching of a critical remote code execution flaw in the Drupal content management system. These updates address severe security issues that could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code remotely on vulnerable servers.

🚀 PHP Security Updates

The PHP dev team released updates for all supported branches, with versions 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, and 8.2.36 now available. Security firm Aikido reports that these updates address 18 CVEs affecting PHP’s core engine, session handling, PHP-FPM, CGI, and other components. The most serious flaw, CVE-2026-129289, is a critical PHP-FPM request smuggling vulnerability with a CVSS score of 9.2. This vulnerability affects certain nginx, Apache, HAProxy, and LSAPI configurations that reuse backend connections to PHP-FPM; standard configurations that do not reuse connections are not affected. As a temporary mitigation, administrators can disable persistent backend connections to ensure they are closed after each request. Third-party maintainer Ondrej Surý has released patched packages for unsupported versions back to PHP 5.6, and Aikido has released hardened container images for similar unsupported versions.

🧩 PHP Vulnerability Details

The following vulnerabilities were fixed in the November updates:

CVE Identifier Description
CVE-2026-129474 Use-after-free vulnerability involving magic method backtraces
CVE-2026-129496 Timezone cache use-after-free vulnerability
CVE-2026-126714 Vulnerability involving partially overwritten session files
CVE-2026-115560 Session serializer mismatch vulnerability
CVE-2026-129291 PHP-FPM epoll use-after-free vulnerability
CVE-2026-128090 PHAR OpenSSL signature bypass vulnerability

Additional fixes address memory corruption, information disclosure, cross-site scripting, denial-of-service issues, and unsafe handling of HTTPS and FTPS URLs. As a temporary mitigation for CVE-2026-115560, PHP recommended disabling session upload progress by setting session.upload_progress.enabled=0. This vulnerability was disclosed in an October 23 informational advisory.

🛡️ Drupal Critical Flaws

The Drupal Security Team has patched a critical remote code execution vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-132165. Discovered by Anthropic’s OSS Scanner, this flaw allows anonymous users to exploit the installer to attempt to reinstall Drupal, potentially leading to site takeover or remote code execution. The security team warned that at least one critical vulnerability can be exploited by anonymous users. Drupal administrators are urged to upgrade to versions 10.6.22, 11.3.22, or 11.4.13. For those who cannot immediately upgrade, it is recommended to secure the Drupal installer by blocking access to /core/install.php in the web server configuration or the .htaccess file. This update also addresses a moderately critical gadget chain vulnerability (CVE-2026-132166). The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has flagged five Drupal vulnerabilities as exploited in the wild since November 2021.

#PHP #Drupal #SecurityUpdates #Vulnerabilities #CVE

Source: PHP security updates fix 18 flaws, including critical RCE bugs Source: Drupal patches critical RCE flaw, warns exploits may surface quickly

item.title: PSF Expands Security Team and Adds New AI Development Entries
item.description:
PSF Expands Security Team and Adds New AI Development Entries

The Python Software Foundation (PSF) has expanded its Developers in Residence program to include three security developers, while recent entries in AI development include running Datasette in the browser and utilizing local large language models.

👥 Security Team Expansion

The PSF operates the Developers in Residence program, which now includes three security developers. One of the new members is Brett Smith. These developers are focused on helping secure Python, PyPI, and the wider ecosystem. The PSF also employs a small staff team to keep operations running, which includes running PyCon US annually and sponsoring core developer sprints.

🧩 Recent AI Development Entries

Recent technical entries document various AI and Python-based developments:

  • Running the full server-side Datasette Python app in the browser using service workers and Pyodide, noted on 17th November 2026.
  • Locating the source of a mysterious beep using Claude, noted on 9th November 2026.
  • Hiding slop PR descriptions behind HTML details tags, noted on 9th November 2026.
  • Running Qwen 3.8 27B on a laptop to interpret model weights, noted on 3rd November 2026.

#Python #AI #Security #Datasette #Pyodide

Source: The PSF end-of-year fundraiser

item.title: Datasette Releases Security Patches Developed with Frontier AI Models
item.description:
Datasette Releases Security Patches Developed with Frontier AI Models

Datasette has released two new security patch versions, 1.0a39 and 0.65.4, following a security audit conducted using frontier AI models.

🚀 Availability

Security fixes are available for the following versions:

  • 1.0a39 (current alpha series)
  • 0.65.4 (stable 0.65.x family)

These patches are recommended for users running Datasette instances on the public web, specifically those mixing public and private tables.

⚙️ Key details

Following issues reported by Sevban Dönmez, Alex Garcia and a collaborator conducted an audit using the following models:

Model Role
Claude Fable 5.1 Security Audit
GPT-5.6 Security Audit
GPT-6 Astra Security Audit

Development of the fixes took place over nearly a week in a shared private repository. For most issues, one person created automated tests to highlight the problem, while the other implemented the fix.

💡 Why it matters

Datasette will be incorporating security audits by frontier models into all of its development work going forward.

#Datasette #Cybersecurity #LLM #SoftwareDevelopment

Source: Datasette 1.0a39 and 0.65.4 security releases
